text: How do you know which network a card belongs to before you ask anyone?

text: Think of a phone number.
prefix: Think of a phone number.

text: Its first digits tell you the country.
prefix: Its first digits tell you the country.

text: They tell you that before anyone answers.
prefix: They tell you that before anyone answers.

text: They never tell you who you are calling.
prefix: They never tell you who you are calling.

text: And a longer code is more exact than a shorter one.
prefix: And a longer code is more exact than a shorter one.

text: A card number works the same way.
prefix: A card number works the same way.

text: Its first digits name the card network and the bank that issued the card.
prefix: Its first digits name the card network and the bank that issued the card.

text: Those first digits are called the BIN, short for bank identification number.
prefix: Those first digits are called the BIN, short for bank identification number.

text: Each network publishes its own list of BINs: which first digits belong to which bank.
prefix: Each network publishes its own list of BINs: which first digits belong to which bank.

text: That is the network's BIN list.
prefix: That is the network's BIN list.

text: The card zone copies those lists in through the adapters.
prefix: The card zone copies those lists in through the adapters.

text: It copies them when it starts, and again on the bank's chosen schedule.
prefix: It copies them when it starts, and again on the bank's chosen schedule.

text: Sometimes a network does not answer, or answers with an empty list.
prefix: Sometimes a network does not answer, or answers with an empty list.

text: Then the card zone keeps its old list.
prefix: Then the card zone keeps its old list.

text: An old list is better than no list.

text: A lookup works like a phone code.
prefix: A lookup works like a phone code.

text: The card zone takes the first eight digits.
prefix: The card zone takes the first eight digits.

text: It tries all eight, then seven, then six.
prefix: It tries all eight, then seven, then six.

text: The longest match wins, because it is the most exact.
prefix: The longest match wins, because it is the most exact.

text: The lookup runs in memory, so it is fast and never touches the database.
prefix: The lookup runs in memory, so it is fast and never touches the database.

text: And the part that knows BINs only ever sees those first eight digits.
prefix: And the part that knows BINs only ever sees those first eight digits.

text: It never sees the whole number.
prefix: It never sees the whole number.

text: An unknown BIN is not an error.
prefix: An unknown BIN is not an error.

text: The answer is simply an empty list.
prefix: The answer is simply an empty list.

text: Why does this matter?

text: Before any network is asked to send a code to a buyer's phone, the card zone checks the card's network this way.
